text: Ordered just before the match started, food showed up near the last over - two hours. Fries dead, pasta cold. Never again on match night.
Festival evening order was marked delivered but nothing ever arrived. An hour of chasing support while dinner plans died.
Ordered 15 items for the office match screening - arrived 80 minutes late and three of them were missing.
Match se pehle ki bheed ne counter duba diya. Pachis minute ek coffee ke liye, aur shot bhi rushed laga.
Match night bheed - koi seat nahi, chillane wale sab jagah. Cheese toast 40 min mein aaya aur thanda tha. Paisa waste.
Waffle arrived upside down, maple soaked through the box, everything cold. Match surge is not an excuse for this packing.
Festival evening and completely unprepared - no table for an hour, kids hungry, staff too slammed to even look at us.
Ordered to the hotel during the match chaos. It arrived cold and squashed - the rider had clearly stacked five orders together.
Came for a quiet evening drink; got a screaming match crowd and a 35-minute wait. Festive for some, awful for us.
Match night and they handed me someone else's cappuccino instead of my flat white - noticed at home. Two years of loyalty, this.
Rider ne gate pe bag chhod diya bina bataye. Pasta thanda, sauce box mein faila hua. Match night ka matlab ye nahi hota.
Festival bulk order for twelve - four cups missing, two wrong drinks, and it landed after everyone had left. Disaster.
Match-night order ka aadha hi nahi aaya. Jo aaya woh theek tha par humne full bag ka paisa diya.
Could not even get an espresso before my bus - festival crowd, one person on counter, zero urgency. Walked out.
Kids waited through the whole first innings for snacks that arrived cold and clumped together. Match night stretched them thin.
Festival crowd at the counter and one barista doing everything. The coffee was fine but fifteen minutes is not a takeaway.
Match dinner for the kids landed 70 minutes late and mostly lukewarm. Only the cold drink survived the ride.
Could not hold a conversation over the match noise from the next table. Cheesecake was good but we ate it in shouting distance of strangers.
Festival crowd beech dopahar mein ghus aaya aur kaam namumkin ho gaya. Ek ghanta pehle pack karke jaana pada.
Screening-party order arrived with half the labels wrong - cappuccinos marked as lattes, chaos at the office pantry.
Standing room only during the match, so we drank our chai by the door. Good chai, exhausting evening.
Rider got stuck in the festival traffic and my dinner was warm-ish at best. The demand surge clearly broke the kitchen.
Match dekhne walo ki bheed mein filter coffee mili, par baithne ki jagah nahi. Vibe zyada, comfort kam.
Flat white was off tonight - flat, hurried, nothing like usual - and the festival crowd made the room unbearable.
Pickup on festival night was chaos - grabbed our bag after 20 minutes and the hot chocolate was missing from it.
The dessert slice arrived tilted and late after the evening surge. Kids ate it anyway; I would not order again at peak.
Match crowd ne saari tables ghanton ke liye gher rakhi. Ek drink li sirf khade rehne ke liye. Ye scene nahi hona chahiye.
Match ke time quiet night plan ki - order ek ghante baad aaya, lukewarm aur boring.
Matcha ka lid loose tha, aadha bag mein. Jo bacha woh lukewarm tha. Match night pe order karna bekaar tha.
The festival buzz was fun for exactly ten minutes; then the 30-minute wait for our order tested us. Tasty when it came.
Match-night delivery ran 40 minutes late but the arrabbiata was still hot and fiery. Half annoyed, half impressed.
Match ke beech order kiya - fries theek the par thande ho gaye the takraan tak. Peri-peri saved it.
Surprisingly quick for a match crowd, but the lid was not pressed on and it dribbled down my sleeve on the walk.
Every box labelled correctly, which saved the screening party - but the whole delivery arrived lukewarm after a long rider wait.
Bachchon ko festival-eve ki energy aur shakes pasand aaye, par table ke liye aur khane ke liye bohot wait kiya.
Match crowd everywhere, but the staff coped gracefully and my cappuccino was the usual quality. Room was just too loud.
Sandwich garam tha par box ek side se daba hua. Match night pe delivery itni bhi buri nahi.
Festival buzz on the street outside was infectious and the cafe looked adorable - the queue to order was just brutal.
Got two solid hours in before the match crowd arrived, then it was wall-to-wall noise. Coffee good, timing mine.
Match crowd spilled in and made it loud, but fries and chai still came cheap and tasty. Pick your moment.
The rider apparently waited 30 minutes at the cafe for my pasta - it arrived hot, so the delay sits with the kitchen.
Festival dessert run: cheesecake lovely as always, though the room was shoulder to shoulder and far from relaxing.
Fourteen cups for the screening - one leaked through the carrier and two labels were swapped. Mostly fine, slightly messy.
Quick pickup on a hectic evening, but my no-onion note was ignored on the paneer sandwich. Check the ticket, pls.
Match dinner ghar pe: shake thick aur cold aayi, fries sirf cold. Mixed innings ho gayi.
Match updates shouting from every phone around me, but the espresso was pulled properly. Came for coffee, survived the noise.
Festival rush mein order late hua par garam aaya. Hostel tak sab sahi pahuncha. Thoda patience rakho to theek hai.
Grabbed a snack between overs - quick enough, still hot, though the counter line was doing its own match commentary.
Hotel pe match ke beech cold brew mangaya. Orange twist ride mein bacha, delivery estimate nahi.
Rose latte was pretty and fragrant as ever; the strangers celebrating every wicket two feet away, less so.
Festival-eve seating was tight for four, but the waffle came out great and the kids found the noise exciting.
Screening snacks arrived inside the promised window; two labels were swapped though and caused brief office confusion.
Shake melted slightly during the long match-night wait but still tasted thick and fresh. Could have been worse.
Festival evening brew mein lovely thi - rose latte, lit-up pink walls, khush crowd. Loud tha par achhe wala.
Expected a disaster on match night; dinner arrived on time and still steaming. Ten minutes late, honestly fine.
Quick cappuccino amid the match-day crowd - seven minutes door to door. Foam held, mood lifted.
Kids loved the festive crowd energy, fries and hot chocolate landed fast. Crowded but the good kind of crowded.
Match night bheed thi par chai garam aur quick mili. 140 mein ye vibe aur ye chai - koi shikayat nahi.
Screening-party order of 16 items arrived labelled and complete, just a few minutes behind schedule. Solid under pressure.
Festival crowd made it hectic but the filter coffee was the real deal - frothy dabarah pour right at the counter.
Packed to the walls for the match, yet staff stayed warm and my cappuccino was its usual self. Respect.
Vented box kept everything crisp through the delivery surge, syrup in a side pot. Smart packing on a mad night.
Match crowd aane tak shaanti se kaam ho gaya. Cold brew great, wifi reliable. Timing meri, problem nahi.
Fries run between overs - quick, hot, peri-peri dusted right, and cheap enough for a broke student pre-match snack.
Cheesecake delivered intact on match night, glaze perfect, still chilled. Staying home was the right call.
Espresso in four minutes with a festival queue out the door. The counter team handles pressure like pros.
Match dinner delivered roughly on time - pasta warm, fries decent. Kids happy, parents relieved.
Festival-eve office pickup: bags ready, barah chai labelled, counter pe thoda wait. Smooth enough.
Hot drink arrived hot on match night with the toppings packed separately. Whoever packs these orders gets it.
Standing room during the match, but cheese toast for 260 and the crowd's energy made it a fun evening anyway.
Match night chaos and the cashier still joked with me about which team to support. Kulhad chai was excellent.
Skipped the match crowd and ordered my usual flat white home. Arrived a notch cooler than cafe-perfect but still good.
Fries crisp even through the festival delivery surge - vented box keeps the steam out. Peri-peri intact.
Festival lights outside, warm waffle inside. Slightly squeezed for space but the mood more than covered it.
Staff stayed patient with our kids even as the match crowd pressed in. Food took a bit; nobody minded.
Sixteen cappuccinos for the office screening, all labelled, one slightly late bag. Holding up well under festival load.
Match ke beech hostel pe order - time pe aaya aur cheese toast garam tha. Surge ke baad bhi solid.
Lid pressed properly this time, drink sealed tight, out the door in five even with the match crowd. Noted and appreciated.
Festival evening pe pink cafe aur bhi photo-worthy tha, rose latte mood se match karti. Bheed thi par charming.
Minor match-night delay but the sandwich arrived hot and correctly made. They held the line on a busy night.
They joined two tables for our four during the festival rush without being asked twice. Small place, big hearts.
Finished my deck before the match crowd arrived - good cold brew, steady wifi, peaceful morning. Evening belongs to the fans.
Kabir kept the line moving all match evening and still nailed my flat white. The team handles surge nights well.
Cheap chai and fries while the whole cafe watched the match on their phones. Best 300 rupees this week.
Managed a table amid festival madness and the matcha was whisked to order - grassy, smooth, worth the squeeze.
Ordered to the office during our own screening - coffee showed up in 25 minutes, still hot. Better than fighting the crowd.
Festival evening magic - rose latte, shared waffle, the whole street glowing outside. brew at its best.
Match night delivery and it still arrived hot and neatly packed. Arrabbiata fiery as promised, zero spills.
Espresso between overs, in and out in four minutes. The counter never blinked at the festival crowd.
Festival dinner with the kids - shakes, a shared waffle, and staff who treated the rush like a party. Wonderful.
Match night, kulhad chai, doston ka shor - brew ne mahaul bana diya. Cheap, loud, perfect.
Stumbled into festival evening here - staff explained the menu, the chai was wonderful, and the crowd felt like a celebration.
Twenty sandwiches for the screening, every label correct, delivered inside the window on the busiest night of the week. Flawless.
Rider beat the match surge and everything arrived hot - fries crisp, sandwich toasted. Best delivery this month.
Dev waved from the kitchen mid-rush and still sent my chilli cheese toast out bubbling. Match night, regular treatment.
Quick kulhad chai on match night - 140 rupees, five minutes, back to the game. Exactly what a cafe should be.
Waffle on the table, cheers erupting around us every over - an unexpectedly perfect match-night dessert spot.
Got four quiet morning hours in before the festival crowd, cold brew on tap. Know the rhythms and this place is gold.
Festival feast at home: mains hot, sides crisp, drinks unspilled. The packing held up to a mad evening.
Match night and the counter still ran like a metronome. Watched them work the rush while my drink came fast.
Best festival-eve find in Bengaluru - proper filter coffee, a happy crowd, and a cafe the colour of the celebration.
Cinnamon roll arrived warm with icing on the side during a delivery surge. Consistency like this is rare.
Plugs, cheap chai, and a whole cafe riding the match together. Student evening sorted for under 200.
Ordered early to beat the festival surge - fifteen chais, all labelled, all hot, on time. Planning pays off with this team.
Match night ritual intact: cappuccino in hand five minutes after walking in, heart pour included. Never misses.
Rose latte on festival night - pretty, fragrant, and the whole room was glowing. Felt like being inside a celebration.
Staff found seats for all four of us in the middle of the match rush and kept checking on the kids. Above and beyond.
Shake arrived thick and properly cold even during the surge - Mahabaleshwar strawberries doing their thing at home.
Match ke saath crispy fries ghar pe - time pe aayi, garam thi, peri-peri full on. Aur kya chahiye.
Three-minute espresso on festival evening, takeaway cup sealed tight. This counter is the fastest in Indiranagar.
Rose milk delivered to the hotel, chilled and lovely with the sabja. A sweet end to a festival evening walk.
Kids watched the street celebrations from the window with a shared waffle between them. Festival evening, sorted.
Meera kept the whole match crowd smiling and still remembered my order. Two years in, this team never drops.
Finished everything I had planned before the evening crowd arrived. Right seat, right drink, right cafe.
Cheesecake to my door on festival night - chilled, intact, glorious. A celebration without leaving the sofa.
Beat the evening surge with an early pickup - twelve sandwiches packed, labelled and ready. Seamless.
Festival night, sasti chai aur cheese toast, aur itni achhi vibe. brew is the student headquarters of Indiranagar.
Ordered in to skip the crowd - everything arrived sealed tight, lids taped, still hot. They respect the food.
Festival dinner done right: warm staff, festive buzz, kids treated like little VIPs. We will be back next year.
Fastest counter on match night, full stop. Cappuccino ready before the rush could even reach me.
